clue.text: Fliers, a couple of which are downloadable from Internet

definitions.text: Fliers, a couple of which are downloadable from Internet

parts.words: Fliers, a couple of which are downloadable from Internet
parts.note: the word Internet holds two coastal birds' names inside it, one starting at its third letter and one at its fourth, so they can be 'downloaded' from it

explanation.walkthrough: 'Downloadable' pretends to be about computer files; really two bird names, TERN and ERNE, are lifted out of the letters of INTERNET.
explanation.definitionFit: Terns and erns are birds of the coast and ocean, so the fliers in question are birds of the sea.

clue.text: Two chaps confused about time -this will show it accurately

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the confused chaps go round the time letter
confused means mixed up, so the letters of two chaps are rearranged

explanation.surface: Two men muddled about the hour need a precise timepiece.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Confused' rearranges TWOCHAPS into STOPWACH; 'about' puts it round T.
explanation.definitionFit: A stopwatch measures elapsed time precisely, so it is a device that shows time accurately.

clue.text: Bishop in a ceremony, with monarch and judge

indicators.note: one piece goes in another, so the bishop's letter sits inside the ceremony

parts.note: a rite is a ceremony
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop
R stands for Rex or Regina, king or queen

explanation.surface: A bishop at a royal ceremony officiating alongside the monarch and a judge.
explanation.definitionFit: An arbiter is one who judges and decides a dispute, so the word is a synonym for judge.

clue.text: Not well employed by business

parts.note: to be in a job is to be employed, as in 'in work'
a firm is a business

explanation.surface: Someone sick working for a company.
explanation.definitionFit: Being infirm means being physically weak or ill, so it is the same as not well.

clue.text: Duke is placed above king or queen say —- shame!

indicators.note: in a down clue, placed above means coming earlier in the column

parts.note: in bridge the ace, king, queen, jack and ten of trumps are called honours

explanation.surface: Scandal as a duke is ranked above the king or queen.
explanation.walkthrough: In card games such as bridge, the top cards are called honours, so 'say' marks king or queen as examples.
explanation.definitionFit: Dishonour is a loss of respect and reputation, which is a disgrace or shame.

clue.text: Travel East with the poet and philosopher

parts.note: to travel is to go
E is the compass abbreviation for East

explanation.surface: An invitation to journey eastwards in the company of a great German writer.
explanation.definitionFit: Goethe, the German author of Faust, was both a poet and a thinker on philosophy and science.

clue.text: What close relative inherits is a book

parts.note: family members inherit genes, the units of heredity passed from parents to children

explanation.surface: A family quarrel over who inherits a particular book.
explanation.definitionFit: Genesis is the first book of the Bible, so it is an example of a book.

clue.text: Bank made to defend our home and employment

parts.note: the Earth is the planet we live on
work is employment

explanation.surface: A call to protect the planet and people's jobs.
explanation.definitionFit: An earthwork is a defensive bank or rampart of soil built up as a fortification.

clue.text: Mostly awful temperature in retreat

indicators.note: mostly means not quite all, so the word for awful loses its final letter

parts.note: hideous means awful

explanation.surface: An almost unbearable heat inside a remote hideaway.
explanation.definitionFit: A hideout is a secret refuge where one can retreat, so the two nouns are synonyms.

clue.text: Part of monarch's regalia monk shortly returned

indicators.note: something returned comes back the way it went, so the short monk is read from right to left

parts.note: a monk is a Brother, abbreviated Bro

explanation.surface: A monk hands back a piece of the royal regalia he had borrowed.
explanation.definitionFit: The sovereign's orb, a jewelled globe topped by a cross, is carried with the sceptre at a coronation.

clue.text: Climb into tree with pole — it could help one secure perch

definitions.text: it could help one secure perch

indicators.note: one piece goes into the other, so the climbing word sits inside the tree

parts.note: a fig is a fruit tree
to shin up is to climb
a rod is a pole

explanation.surface: Advice to shin up a tree with a pole, as if for an acrobatic perch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Perch' looks like a place to sit after climbing a tree; it is the freshwater fish an angler hopes to land.
explanation.definitionFit: An angler uses this rod and line to catch fish such as perch, so it helps one secure a perch.

clue.text: Flood most of battlefield — good!

indicators.note: taking most of a word means dropping its last letter, here from the battlefield

parts.note: Waterloo, in Belgium, is the battlefield where Napoleon was defeated in 1815

explanation.surface: A cheer at the prospect of flooding most of a historic battlefield.
explanation.definitionFit: To waterlog ground is to saturate it with water until it is flooded and sodden.

clue.text: Coach a lot of swimmers

definitions.meaning: to coach is to train or teach
a large group of fish swimming together is a shoal, also called by this name

explanation.definitionFit: To school is to coach or train, and a school is a collective noun for a large group of fish.

clue.text: Call to give expected time of delivery

definitions.meaning: to call something by a name is to designate or name it
the full length of a pregnancy, ending on the due date of a baby's birth

explanation.surface: Someone phoning to tell a customer when a parcel should arrive.
explanation.definitionFit: To term is to call or name something, and a pregnancy carried to term reaches the expected birth date.

clue.text: Parked in wrong position, is clamped, disastrously

indicators.note: disastrously suggests things going badly wrong, so the letters are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: A badly parked car gets clamped, to the driver's dismay.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Disastrously' rearranges ISCLAMPED; the definition is the first four words.
explanation.definitionFit: Something misplaced has been put in the wrong place, as a car parked in the wrong position.

clue.text: Value of small piece of poetry for poet

parts.note: a word, here with possessive 's from 'of', is a small piece of a poem
worth is value

explanation.surface: Someone asks what a brief scrap of verse is really worth to a poet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Of' marks a possessive: the value of a word is a word's worth, so the value comes last though printed first. The definition is the final word, 'poet'.
explanation.definitionFit: William Wordsworth was the English Romantic poet who wrote about daffodils and the Lake District.

clue.text: Where partners relax with duplicate bridge every day, initially

parts.note: to double is to duplicate

indicators.note: initially picks out the opening letter of each of the three words before it

explanation.surface: Couples unwind each day by playing duplicate bridge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Duplicate bridge' and 'partners' suggest the card game; the partners are a couple in bed.
explanation.definitionFit: A double bed is made for two people, so it is where a couple of partners rest.

clue.text: Reluctance to reformulate any ethics

indicators.note: to reformulate is to make up again, so the letters are reworked into a fresh order

explanation.surface: Unwillingness to rewrite any code of ethics.
explanation.definitionFit: Hesitancy is an unwillingness or hesitation to act, which is the same as reluctance.

clue.text: Pursuing impressive domestic policy?

parts.note: read as politics this is a government's home agenda, but it describes someone whose aim is a home that impresses visitors

explanation.walkthrough: 'Domestic policy' suggests a government's home affairs; it is a person's policy of keeping a spotless, impressive house.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone house-proud takes great pride in the tidiness and appearance of their home, aiming to impress.

clue.text: For Cockney, really fashionable dance

indicators.note: Cockney speech drops the H sound at the start of words, so both words lose their opening letter

parts.note: honest, as in 'honest, I did', means really
hep is old slang for fashionable, a variant of hip

explanation.surface: A Londoner describes a dance as truly trendy.
explanation.walkthrough: A Cockney is a working-class Londoner, famous for dropping initial H, so 'honest' and 'hep' become 'ONEST and 'EP.
explanation.definitionFit: The one-step was a quick ballroom dance of the early twentieth century, one step to each beat.

clue.text: People of North America, those willing to take pledge

definitions.meaning: a Native American people of the Great Plains, in present-day Nebraska and Kansas
a pawnee is the person to whom a pledge is pawned, as a pawnbroker is

explanation.surface: Native Americans signing up to take a pledge, perhaps of abstinence.
explanation.definitionFit: The Pawnee are a Plains nation, and in law a pawnee is someone who takes a pawned pledge.

clue.text: Weapon knight turned on king

indicators.note: in an across clue, put on means placed after, so the turned title follows the king

parts.note: K is the chess and card abbreviation for king

indicators.note: turned round, the knight's title is read backwards

parts.note: a knight is addressed as Sir

explanation.surface: A knight turns his weapon on the king in a palace revolt.
explanation.definitionFit: A kris is a Malay dagger with a wavy blade, so it is a kind of weapon.

clue.text: Again accept in US college, having studied first

indicators.note: first puts the studying piece ahead of the college in the column

parts.note: to read a subject at university is to study it
MIT is the Massachusetts Institute of Technology

explanation.surface: Readmission to an American college for someone who studied there before.
explanation.definitionFit: To readmit someone is to let them in again, so the verb means to accept again.

clue.text: Monk and I altered old robe

indicators.note: altered means changed, so the letters of monk and I are rearranged

explanation.surface: A monk and the speaker adjust an old robe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Altered' turns MONKI into KIMON, and O follows.
explanation.definitionFit: A kimono is a long loose Japanese robe with wide sleeves, tied with a sash.

clue.text: Chicken or what it comes from, partly

definitions.meaning: chicken as an adjective means cowardly
a chicken comes from an egg, and part of an egg is its golden centre, sometimes called by this colour name

explanation.surface: The old chicken-and-egg puzzle, with a nod to which came first.
explanation.definitionFit: Cowardly people are called yellow, and the yolk of an egg is also known as its yellow.

clue.text: Person demanding right ain't calm, originally

indicators.note: taken as 'in an original way', these letters are arranged afresh

explanation.surface: Someone who demands their rights is anything but calm at first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Originally' looks as if it wants first letters; here it signals a fresh arrangement of AINT and CALM.
explanation.definitionFit: A claimant is a person who makes a claim, demanding something as a right, such as benefit or compensation.

clue.text: Issue penalty to bad boyo, namely fine

parts.note: to ticket a motorist is to issue a penalty notice

indicators.note: bad suggests the boyo is messed up, so its letters are disordered

explanation.surface: A traffic warden fines a Welsh lad for bad behaviour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bad' turns BOYO into YBOO. Boyo is Welsh slang for a lad; tickety-boo is old British slang for all right.
explanation.definitionFit: Tickety-boo is chirpy British slang meaning fine, in good order, all well.

clue.text: Provide with crew from island

definitions.meaning: to supply a ship or post with people to run it
the Isle of ... lies in the Irish Sea between Britain and Ireland

explanation.definitionFit: To man a ship is to provide it with crew, and Man is the island in the Irish Sea.

clue.text: In this suit is at high level

definitions.text: In this suit is at high level

parts.words: In this suit is at high level
parts.note: the phrase 'in' plus the name of a card suit is an idiom meaning to a great degree, in abundance

explanation.walkthrough: Being 'in' this card suit means having something at a high level, as in 'trouble in abundance'.
explanation.definitionFit: Spades is the highest-ranking suit in bridge, and doing something in spades means doing it to a high degree.

clue.text: Skilfully converted from idolatry

indicators.note: converted from means changed out of, so the letters are rebuilt into a new word

explanation.surface: Someone skilfully talked out of idol worship.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something adroitly means doing it deftly and with dexterity, which is the same as skilfully.
